literal: Pallor saying name obtaining is good indeed, he who caused love's not granting they slander not if.
translation: It is good indeed to be known merely as "the pale one", as long as people do not slander the unkindness of the one who made me love him.
modern: என் மீது அன்பு கொள்ளச் செய்த காதலர் இப்போது எனக்கு அன்பு காட்டாததை ஊரார் பழித்துத் தூற்றமாட்டார்கள் என்றால், நான் பசலை நோய் கொண்டவள் என்று பெயர் பெறுவது எனக்கு நல்லதே ஆகும்.
explanation: The heroine is suffering from the physical signs of lovesickness, known as pallor, because her lover is away. She knows that the townspeople will notice her condition and gossip about it. However, she prefers that they simply label her condition as a disease called "pallor" rather than blaming her lover for his absence and lack of grace. This shows her deep devotion, as she is willing to bear the physical suffering and the stigma of the illness as long as her lover's reputation remains untarnished.
